profile.reading: This is one of eleven OpenStreetMap points sharing the identical name Blockfusion Niagra Falls, all located at or near 5380 Frontier Avenue in Niagara Falls, New York, most plausibly representing separate structures within a single campus operated by BlockFusion USA, Inc. rather than eleven genuinely distinct facilities. BlockFusion, founded in 2019 by CEO Alex Martini-Lo Manto and COO Kant Trivedi, converted a retired coal-burning power plant at this address into a cryptocurrency mining hosting campus that is increasingly pivoting toward artificial intelligence and high-performance-computing colocation. The site draws roughly 90 percent of its power from carbon-free hydroelectric generation supplied by the nearby Robert Moses Niagara Hydroelectric Power Station, according to a 2022 SEC filing by hosting customer Bit Digital, Inc., a publicly traded Bitcoin mining company. A second major customer, Gryphon Digital Mining, Inc., signed a colocation agreement effective December 1, 2024, hosting nearly 5,000 mining machines on 12 megawatts of power. As of BlockFusion's most recent disclosures, the campus has 46 megawatts of Tier 1 power currently energized, with more than 100 additional megawatts of Tier 3 capacity planned as part of an AI and HPC-focused expansion developed with architecture and engineering firms Gensler, JB&B, and Thornton Tomasetti. In November 2025, BlockFusion announced plans to go public through a merger with special-purpose acquisition company Blue Acquisition Corp, becoming Blockfusion Data Centers, Inc. under ticker BLDC, in a deal valuing the company at 450 million dollars pre-money, a transaction still pending as of the most recent regulatory filing found. The underlying colocation contract with Gryphon describes the site as including both mobile container-based mining units and indoor pod space within larger main buildings, a documented, phased-construction pattern that plausibly explains why multiple separate structures were mapped at this one campus rather than indicating genuinely distinct facilities.

reading.body:
The Blockfusion Niagara Falls campus currently operates 46 megawatts of IT-ready power drawn largely from the Robert Moses hydroelectric station, with plans to expand to over 100 megawatts. At typical AI training density of 40 kilowatts per rack, the current 46 megawatts of IT load translates to roughly 1,150 racks, or enough for several thousand high-end accelerators depending on configuration; the planned capacity would support roughly 2,500 racks. The site is Tier 1 certified for current operations and Tier 3 for the planned expansion, indicating it qualifies for mission-critical colocation workloads.

This campus ranks second by published capacity among the 31 facilities mapped in New York State, though the state has disclosed power figures for only one other facility beyond this one. Blockfusion converted a retired coal plant to create the site in 2019 and has shifted focus from cryptocurrency hosting toward AI and high-performance-computing colocation in its recent expansion. The operator has announced a pending merger with Blue Acquisition Corp valued at 450 million dollars pre-money as of November 2025.

Access to hydroelectric power at roughly 90 percent of supply gives this site an energy cost and carbon profile distinct from most US data center regions. The planned 100-megawatt expansion represents a significant bet that the site can retain and grow computational workload as AI demand reshapes hosting markets. Whether that expansion reaches planned scale depends on factors not published here: power supply commitments from the utility, customer appetite for the location, and whether the pending SPAC merger closes.
